newsitem.title: UK: Academics,industry to educate UK public on finance.
newsitem.headline: Academics,industry to educate UK public on finance.

text.p: No amount of regulation will protect British investors adequately unless it is accompanied by moves to educate both adults and children on the pitfalls of personal finance, a group of academics and industry participants warned on Thursday.

Chris Green, director of the Consumer Finance Education Centre at the University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology (UMIST), said education and regulation needed to be linked and it was clear the case for education had been made by recent financial scandals.

Green was speaking at the launch of the new consumer finance centre, which has been established on a charitable non-profit basis with financial support of 210,000 pounds from 14 founding sponsors, including 13 financial services organisations.

These include building societies such as Bradford & Bingley, Nationwide and Britannia as well as the Royal Bank of Scotland and the Co-operative Bank and life assurers such as Commercial Union Life and General Accident Life.
UMIST principal Bob Boucher said customers did not trust financial services.

"With the private sector expected to play an increasing role in the financial well-being of the public in years to come, this is not a healthy situation," he told a briefing at the annual meeting of the Building Societies Association (BSA), one of the new centre's sponsors.

The centre aims to raise public knowledge and understanding about borrowing, saving and investing as well as planning for retirement and insuring against risk. This will, its backers said, empower consumers and make them better informed for choices on money matters, so enhancing consumer protection.

"This is in the enlightened self-interest of every organisation in this industry," Green said. He said the centre would be wholly independent and would not pander to the public relations agenda put forward by financial services providers.
